conventions.convention: Use four-dimensional Minkowski space with metric diag(-1,1,1,1), natural units c=ℏ=1, derivative weight one, and explicitly assigned rational field weights. Both jet order and polynomial field degree are bounded.
The polynomial algebra is Sym(J_even*) tensor Λ(J_odd*); even generators commute, odd generators anticommute, and the induced left action is (g·f)(z)=f(ρ(g⁻¹)z).
The quotient is V_D/R_D, where V_D=W_D^G and R_D is the intersection of the explicitly specified G-stable raw relation space with V_D. It records only the declared relations.
Invariant-quotient exactness assumes full AC, a complex reductive affine algebraic group, a finite-dimensional rational module, and a G-stable relation subspace.

Admitted currents and variations have compact support; integrated total divergences vanish. The Euler derivative is characterized by DS₀[φ](h)=I(Σ hᵃEₐ⁽⁰⁾), with the stated ordering for odd fields. The removal map is Ψ_k=id−εᵏF.

Odd integration extracts the coefficient of ξ₁⋯ξ_n in that order; odd sources precede field coordinates in the source pairing, and odd source derivatives are left graded derivatives. Every change of variables must satisfy the exact integration identity with its full Jacobian and transformed source.

LSZ comparisons use supplied positive-mass stable simple poles, a common invertible overlap matrix, fixed choices z_a²=Z_a, and existing common regulator and joint-residue limits. These existence conditions are assumptions, not constructed QFT results.
The scalar example adjoins a formal mass symbol M_s of weight one before forming homogeneous polynomials and specializes M_s=m afterward; ε²=0.

load_bearing.statement: A local operator in this finite-order data is an element of P_{r,q,D} evaluated at x on the r-jet of the fields. A scalar operator invariant under the declared symmetries is an element of V_{r,q,D}=P_{r,q,D}^G.

The finite-order invariant operator-basis quotient is Q_D:=V_D/R_D. Two invariant operators represent the same class exactly when their difference lies in R_D. An operator basis is any finite list of representatives in V_D of a vector-space basis of Q_D.

The normalized LSZ amplitude is the joint residue, multiplied by the product of the chosen inverse square roots of external-pole residues. The joint limits, Fourier transforms, pole factorization and invertible overlap data must all exist as part of the supplied LSZ datum.

Under the stated exact regulated change-of-variables identity, full transformed action, graded Jacobian and transformed source, unit partition values, and common stable-pole LSZ data, Z'_{ρ,ε}[J]=Z_{ρ,ε}[J] coefficientwise in R_N, and the normalized on-shell LSZ amplitudes agree coefficientwise modulo ε^{N+1}.

Assume AC. For a finite-dimensional rational module V of a complex reductive affine algebraic group G and a G-stable subspace N, the restriction V^G→(V/N)^G is surjective with kernel V^G∩N; hence V^G/(V^G∩N)→(V/N)^G is a canonical complex-linear isomorphism.

Under the stated finite-jet, action, compact-support, variation and formal-truncation hypotheses, Ψ_k(φ)=φ−εᵏF[φ] is formally invertible through order N and S_ε[Ψ_k(φ)]=S_ε[φ]−εᵏI(FᵃEₐ⁽⁰⁾[φ])+O(ε^{k+1}). All induced terms through the retained order must be kept.

For finite-dimensional graded J, finite polynomial-degree bound q and rational target weight D, the span P_{q,D} of supercommutative monomials of degree at most q and weight D is finite-dimensional; its invariant subspace is also finite-dimensional for a parity- and weight-preserving group action.

published_dependencies.used_for: The complex reductive-group hypothesis and its fixed-vector definition of unipotence in the local-operator definition and invariant-exactness lemma.

Clause (ii), specifically surjectivity on invariant vectors for a surjective equivariant rational-module map, as cited by the invariant-quotient lemma. Its AC and complex-reductivity hypotheses are retained.
The explicitly adopted full-AC premise in invariant exactness, the action-level redundancy proposition, and the scalar example's prerequisite chain.

alerts.finding: The Example states 'Let m≥0 be a fixed mass spurion of engineering weight one' and declares a 'dimension-six relation subspace' containing φ³(□−m²)φ. Verification 1.1 calls this generator homogeneous of weight six. The cited finite-jet supplier defines a polynomial algebra over C graded by its jet generators; a fixed numerical coefficient m² does not change the weight-four monomial φ⁴ into weight six. The example does not explicitly adjoin a formal mass generator or define an enlarged graded coefficient algebra before specializing m. Thus, for m≠0, membership of this relation in the cited fixed-weight space needs justification. Batch 16's ex-aqft-operator-basis-reduction explicitly separates a formal symbol M_s from its numerical specialization, illustrating the missing algebraic distinction. The action calculation itself is unaffected.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite is listed on the page, but the assigned items make no load-bearing citation to its items. The exterior-algebra and graded-source conventions are defined locally; no stronger foundation theorem is attributed to this page.

The physical operator contract retains finite jet and degree bounds, explicitly declared stable relation spaces, and the quotient's limited scope. It separately requires compatibility with physical symmetries and does not infer amplitude equivalence.

The zero-derivative scalar-gauge example preserves the supplier's scope. The scalar EOM example has the fixed numerical mass versus homogeneous polynomial-space mismatch reported in alerts; its direct action substitution is sound.

The Warsaw contract treats its classification as a literature-defined list and the local quotient as a formal selection, without claiming a locally proved completeness classification. Chiral counting is explicitly separated from canonical engineering weight and from finite polynomial SMEFT lists.

The scattering-channel definition uses the finite scalar jet and engineering-weight convention for O₈, specifies its Lorentz action, and expressly makes no basis-independence claim for C₈. Exact matching and omitted contributions remain separate supplied data.

The Wilsonian-action definition retains declared quotient relations and separately requires the regulated map, inverse, full Jacobian, transformed source, and common stable positive-mass LSZ data for amplitude equivalence. Its additional AC assumption strengthens rather than weakens the amplitude theorem's hypotheses.

The scheme definition uses a supplied finite fixed-weight quotient and ordered basis only. It excludes completeness claims, treats RG equations as additional supplied data, and explicitly restricts this application to nonzero quotient dimension.

The quartic contact-jet proposition imposes an additional certificate on the actual relation space before descending its contact map. It proves annihilation of certified relations directly and does not identify the quotient with a full amplitude or infer positivity of an isolated perturbative contribution.
